citations.narrative:
The licensee did not notify Animal Care of significant business changes 90 days prior to said changes and did not obtain a
new license before these changes occurred. Substantial business changes include changes such as in business or
operation, locations, and activities. The licensee reports the pet store that was licensed under a "Class B" license closed
more than 1 year ago. The licensee now houses animals at a new location and conducts regulated business that falls
under the classification of a "Class C" license (exhibiting). Correct by ensuring all significant business changes be
reported to Animal Care at least 90 days in advance of any changes and that the proper licensure has been obtained prior
to conducting regulated business. Correct by: November 30, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the licensee.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
